rows.A_note: EV-030 puts AI risk inside the enterprise framework and EV-031 is an approved appetite statement. Coverage of all register categories is unevidenced, EV-032 shows 2 of 6 risks with no escalation history, and EV-033 is a single escalation. Level 3 quantitative thresholds and a dashboard are absent.
rows.B_note: Appetite statement and thresholds exist and are approved, but no evidence of quantitative dashboard or scheduled review.

rows.A_note: Level 2 is supported by EV-040 (scheduled plan), EV-043 (KPI per clause) and EV-042 (findings tracker with closures). Q1 covered only 9 of 12 clauses and 5 open findings lack target dates, but the plan covers all 12 clauses and Q2 reached 12 of 12. EV-043 and EV-044 are close to level 3, but one KPI report is not a cadence and no body receives the reports, so the score stays at 2.
rows.B_note: KPIs are measured and reported against targets for each policy, but no evidence of continuous enforcement or independent audit.

rows.A_note: EV-100 (charter, quarterly cadence), EV-101 (3 minuted meetings) and EV-102 (decisions log) support a chartered committee with recorded decisions. The portfolio-coverage clause has no named artefact and cannot be inferred from the others, so it scores level 1. Level 3 (a decided-versus-noted measure) and level 4 (board reporting and a strategy change, with EV-103 showing strategy is outside the co
rows.B_note: Committee charter, minutes, and decisions log exist, but no measure of items decided versus noted.

rows.A_note: The absence of AI-specific monitoring is established. EV-120 is an all-staff dashboard and EV-121 is one paragraph on technical roles, neither AI-specific. Level 1 is not evidenced because the pack names no non-discrimination policy, so the score is 0, not NA.
rows.B_note: Diversity data is not AI-specific and no action plans or progress reviews exist.

rows.A_note: EV-171 shows individual-driven engagement without an agreement, which fits level 1 exactly. EV-170 says no formal partnership exists and does not conflict with it.
rows.B_note: Absence is established by EV-170

rows.A_note: EV-620, EV-621 and EV-623 would support levels 2 and 3 for the 14 registered systems. The open exception in EV-622 means coverage fails, so level 1.
rows.B_note: Metrics and review exist, but not for every deployment

rows.A_note: The inventory (EV-710, EV-712) covers all 14 systems with versions and change notifications. Monthly drift metrics (EV-713) are present, but the missed evaluation breaks level 2, so level 3 cannot be credited.
rows.B_note: Coverage fails: not all version changes are evaluated, so level 3 not fully satisfied.

rows.A_note: EV-730 and EV-731 evidence the monitoring-to-release link. Under one artefact, one clause, the stakeholder and best-practice clauses are unevidenced. EV-732 covers effect for only 7 of 9 releases with no cadence or reporting body, so level 3 would also fail.
rows.B_note: Coverage fails: not all releases have measured effect recorded.

rows.A_note: The strategy is documented and board-approved (EV-220), which exceeds level 1. Cadence fails the two-minuted-occurrences test. KPIs (EV-222) are defined, but there is no board reporting cadence evidence, so level 3 also fails.
rows.B_note: Cadence fails: only one occurrence of KPI reporting, not a cadence.

rows.A_note: The documentation clause (EV-330) and the one-off effectiveness assessment (EV-332) are present, but under one artefact per clause, alignment is unevidenced. The 38% 'appropriate' override rating is unactioned. Level 3 per-system rates are not reported.
rows.B_note: Cadence not met: only one effectiveness assessment, not on a stated cadence.

rows.A_note: EV-400, EV-401 and EV-402 support anchor 2. The coverage report (EV-403) is quarterly but shows one minuted review, so the cadence test fails. The pack names no separate validation artefact for the 'validated metrics' clause (the only study is in MEA-1.2), and anchor 2 is credited on that basis.
rows.B_note: Boundary at level 3: coverage report and review on cadence evidenced, but no external validation or science revision.

rows.A_note: EV-412 (false-positive/false-negative analysis and revision history for all 9 metrics) is anchor 3 content. EV-413 does not state that all 9 metrics were re-validated, so anchor 2 coverage is unproven and the score stays at 1.
rows.B_note: Boundary at level 3: revision history and false-positive/negative analysis evidenced, but no research contribution or continuous optimisation.

rows.A_note: EV-430 and EV-431 show good practice for recent runs. Coverage is not 100%, so anchor 2 fails. The 9/12 reproducibility figure has no stated target or reporting body, so it would not satisfy anchor 3 either.
rows.B_note: Boundary at level 3: reproducibility measured and reported, but no automation or research-grade/public methodology.

rows.A_note: CTA evidence (EV-530 to EV-533) would reach anchor 3 on its own, but coverage across in-scope systems fails at anchor 2. The score is capped at 1 by the coverage rule.
rows.B_note: Coverage definition: only CTA system evidenced, not all in-scope systems.

rows.A_note: EV-440 to EV-442 show there is no ethics process, but no study ran without one. Anchor 0 (studies run without review) is not established, so the score is NA rather than 0.
rows.B_note: Absence established: no human-subject evaluation or ethics process exists.

rows.A_note: Level 2 is met by EV-460 (all 14 in-scope systems) and EV-461. Level 3 fails the MEASURE and CADENCE tests. EV-463 supports predictive alerting and threshold re-setting, but level 4 cannot be credited while level 3 is incomplete and no real-time dashboard artefact exists.

The content of EV-480 (fail-safe tests) and EV-481 (residual risks accepted by the Model Owner) would satisfy level 2 for the evaluated system. Coverage is unevidenced. EV-482 shows no periodic re-test, and level 3 threshold tracking is absent.
rows.B_note: EV-482 confirms no periodic re-test or tracking

rows.A_note: Level 2 rests on EV-500 (dated transparency risk assessment) and EV-501 (approved member notice and adverse-action letters with top-2 reasons). EV-502 limits scope to CTA, and the anchor has no 'every system' clause. The accountability-risk and adequacy clauses are thinly evidenced, so this is a close level-2 call.
rows.B_note: Coverage definition not met

rows.A_note: Ongoing tracking with a named owner exceeds the level-1 failure conditions, but register coverage is unevidenced and the cadence has a gap. EV-562 shows only 7 of 23 entries closed, and level 3 time-to-log measures are absent.
rows.B_note: EV-561 shows one missed review, but cadence is otherwise met; no measurement of tracking coverage or time-to-log

rows.A_note: Problem reporting (EV-580) and appeals (EV-581) exist, which is beyond level 1. Integration is unevidenced and a clause cannot be inferred from another artefact, so the score is the level below. Feedback volume and appeal counts are present without targets.
rows.B_note: EV-582: analysis not published, no linkage to system changes

rows.A_note: Level 2 is met by EV-610 and EV-611 (both declines detected, with root cause and fix recorded) and EV-613 (process applied to all 14 systems). Level 3 fails the MEASURE test because no target is stated, and no predictive modelling is evidenced for level 4.
rows.B_note: EV-612: detection latency and change-to-action time measured, but no predictive modelling
